# Quantum Leap Energy and Necsa Sign Binding Heads of Agreement to Establish Joint Venture for HALEU Production in South Africa


October 15, 2026 • 8:00 AM EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_059edd6164555779fa5741a1955aca83/aspisotopes/news/2026-10-15_Quantum_Leap_Energy_and_Necsa_Sign_Binding_Heads_120.pdf)


*Joint Venture Supported by Offtake Agreements with TerraPower, Initial Regulatory Approvals, and Access to Site Infrastructure to enable QLE and Necsa to Advance Toward Commercial-Scale HALEU Production*


DALLAS, Oct. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ASP Isotopes Inc. (NASDAQ: ASPI) ("ASPI") today announced that a subsidiary of Quantum Leap Energy LLC ("QLE," the "Company" or “Quantum Leap Energy”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of ASPI, has signed a Heads of Agreement (the "Agreement") with the Nuclear Energy Corporation of South Africa SOC Limited ("Necsa"). The Agreement establishes a binding commercial framework for a joint venture between QLE and Necsa (the “Joint Venture”) to develop, finance, construct, commission, own, and operate a test bench and commercial-scale facility for the production of High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium ("HALEU") at Necsa's Pelindaba site in South Africa.


"The world needs new, reliable and secure sources of advanced nuclear fuel, and South Africa is well placed to provide them," said Loyiso Tyabashe, Group Chief Executive Officer of Necsa. “Through this partnership with Quantum Leap Energy, Necsa will bring its decades of experience in nuclear operations, safeguards and regulatory compliance to creating a trusted new source of commercial HALEU supply.”


The Agreement marks a significant step forward in QLE's relationship with Necsa, building on the Memorandum of Understanding signed in November 2024 and the Pre-Implementation Services Contract signed in February 2026. Meaningful progress has already been made on the ground. In July 2026, QLE received approval from South Africa's Ministry of Electricity and Energy to acquire, possess, use, dispose of and transport source material and nuclear related equipment and technology to advance uranium enrichment activities at Pelindaba. At Pelindaba, a test bench facility was previously constructed, and the refurbishment of the infrastructure housing the test bench is currently underway, while engagements with the relevant authorities have commenced. Further, QLE has already secured offtake for the HALEU the Joint Venture is expected to produce through supply agreements with TerraPower, one of the world's leading advanced nuclear reactor developers.


"This agreement demonstrates real commercial progress and brings us one step closer to enrichment," said Dr. Ryno Pretorius, Chief Executive Officer of Quantum Leap Energy. “We are proud to be working alongside Necsa, whose nuclear site, infrastructure and expertise no other partner could replicate. With offtake from TerraPower already in place, we are positioned to deliver the HALEU that will fuel the next generation of nuclear reactors.”


Under the agreed principles, QLE will hold approximately 80% of the ownership interest in the Joint Venture and lead operations and the arrangement of capital. Necsa will hold approximately 20% of the Joint Venture and contribute site access, nuclear safeguards support, and licensing and regulatory support that are essential to progressing HALEU production in South Africa.


As the statutory nuclear energy institution of the Republic of South Africa, Necsa brings deep nuclear expertise, infrastructure, regulatory relationships and licensing capability to the Joint Venture. Necsa is headquartered at Pelindaba, South Africa's premier nuclear research center, home to the 20MW SAFARI-1 research reactor and the site of more than six decades of nuclear activity. The parties also intend for Necsa to enter an engineering, procurement and construction arrangement with QLE, giving the project direct access to Necsa's engineering capabilities. QLE believes that combining its proprietary enrichment technology with Necsa's established nuclear platform offers a highly efficient route to commercial HALEU production.


**About Quantum Leap Energy**
Quantum Leap Energy is a development-stage nuclear fuels company dedicated to advancing innovative technologies and processes across critical segments of the nuclear fuel cycle. The company focuses on uranium conversion, enrichment of uranium-235 for nuclear fuel production (HALEU, LEU+ and LEU), and isotopic separation of lithium-6 and lithium-7, as well as radioactive waste treatment technologies. Through exclusive global rights to proprietary Aerodynamic Separation Process (ASP) and laser-based Quantum Enrichment (QE) technologies, Quantum Leap Energy aims to address perceived gaps in the nuclear fuel supply chain for advanced nuclear reactors, small modular reactors, and fusion systems. The company has established strategic partnerships or commercial initiatives and relationships with industry leaders including TerraPower, Fermi America, and the South Africa Nuclear Energy Corporation (Necsa) to accelerate the commercialization of critical isotopes essential for next-generation nuclear energy systems. *The company has not applied its enrichment technologies to the enrichment of U-235, nor received permission or regulatory approval to conduct testing of our enrichment technologies on U-235, except for the activities contemplated by the services contract with Necsa. **About ASP Isotopes Inc.**
ASP Isotopes Inc. is an advanced materials company focused on developing technologies and processes for the production of critical materials used in multiple industries, including nuclear medicine, electronics and nuclear energy. The Company's proprietary Aerodynamic Separation Process ("ASP technology") and Quantum Enrichment ("QE technology") are designed to enable the production of isotopes for a range of industrial and advanced technology applications. The Company operates isotope enrichment facilities in Pretoria, South Africa, focused on low atomic mass elements, or light isotopes, and a gas production facility in Free State Province, South Africa, focused on liquid natural gas and liquid helium. For more information, please visit[www.aspisotopes.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=cc2iQQtsGPVcsOHlsPuZoGvsn2YclnA3wW3Wn-FGjaM6GhAQW6Juyfl-uQ9X0xWfsekwJd3E-Z1lc7Eezeb-GsV5kk--JXVv0ALAsSQSmqU=) .
